The group that makes up **at least 70 % of the world’s Jewish population** is the **Ashkenazi Jews**.  
Genome‑wide studies often find that Ashkenazim cluster with Italians because they share **two major ancestries**:

| Factor | What it explains |
|--------|------------------|
| **Levantine/ ancient Israelite ancestry** | Both Ashkenazi Jews and many Italians (especially from the south) carry a substantial proportion of DNA that traces back to ancient peoples of the Levant – the original homeland of the Israelite tribes. |
| **Southern‑European/ Italian gene flow** | Over many centuries, Jews living in Roman and later Italian society intermarried with local populations, adding a sizable southern‑European component to the Ashkenazi gene pool. |

The overlap of these Levantine and Southern‑European ancestries is why genomics analyses often place Ashkenazi Jews in close genetic proximity to Italians, even though the Ashkenazi population also retains distinct European and Eastern‑European signals.
